messages:
carla_support: Heads-up — AcmeAnalytics escalated. Their API calls with x-preferred-region=eu-west-1 are failing auth and getting routed to us-west-2 after a 503 fallback. Customer sees 3–5s tails and large cross-region egress billing. Repro + logs below.

ben_infra: can you paste a minimal repro curl? also which VIP/service?

carla_support: VIP is api-prod-usv1 (load-balancer vip). repro loop: 
```bash
for i in {1..5}; do \
  curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-preferred-region: eu-west-1' \
    'https://api.example.com/v1/query' -w '\n--END--\n'; sleep 1;
done
```
Responses: first request -> HTTP/1.1 200 (served from eu pool A, header x-origin-region: eu-west-1)
second request -> HTTP/1.1 503 (pool A health transient), subsequent requests -> HTTP/1.1 200 but served from us pool B and x-origin-region header is MISSING. Auth backend rejects tokens due to region-scoped keys -> 401s in app logs.

edgebot: svc-router: vip api-prod-usv1 -> pool-a (eu-west-1) failed TCP healthcheck; fallback to pool-b (us-west-2). route-id=vip-prod-usv1/route-23; applied fallback policy: L7-failover-v1.

dave_sre: I reproduced locally against the VIP. Quick debug: when failover triggers we pass through a small filter that rebuilds response headers; it strips unrecognized upstream headers by default. Looks like x-origin-region is not whitelisted in that rewrite. That causes downstream auth to treat request as cross-region.

ben_infra: where is the header whitelist configured now? IIRC we added env var ROUTE_HEADER_ALLOWLIST in the L7 proxy config but a follow-up change gated it for non-2xx responses.

carla_support: attaching a snippet from the proxy logs showing header removal: 
```
[2026-02-13T14:12:33Z] route=vip-prod-usv1 pool=pool-a resp=503 upstream_headers={date,server,content-type} -> fallback pool=pool-b upstream_headers_after_fallback={date,server,content-type}
[2026-02-13T14:12:34Z] route=vip-prod-usv1 pool=pool-b resp=200 upstream_headers={date,server,content-type}
```
No x-origin-region anywhere after failover.

sre-rotation: this fits the pattern we saw in last week's patch (PR 4512) where we tightened header sanitation for non-2xx paths. We probably forgot to include any x-* region headers.

ben_infra: quick mitigation options: 
- restore previous header pass-through for failover paths (config flip)
- add x-preferred-region cookie sticky routing to avoid immediate fallback for the short window
- server-side: make auth tolerant to absent region header (longer term).

maya_prod: customerImpact: high (auth 401s + latency + egress). Legal/compliance wants a timeline and mitigation ASAP. Can we do a 10% canary config flip for api-prod-usv1?

dave_sre: I have a patch: set preserve_upstream_headers_for_fallback: true in route config and add x-origin-region to allowed_headers list. Patch ready: 
```yaml
routes:
  - id: vip-prod-usv1
    fallback: L7-failover-v1
    preserve_upstream_headers_for_fallback: true
    allowed_headers: [date, server, content-type, x-origin-region, x-request-id]
```
I can deploy canary to 10% in 20m.

edgebot: deploy-bot: starting canary for route vip-prod-usv1 -> 10% (deploy id dpl-2026-02-13-77).

carla_support: assigning owner: ben_infra. Please keep me posted; customer requests ETA and whether we can retroactively credit cross-region egress.

ben_infra: I'll own. Immediate plan: run canary, monitor for missing x-origin-region in fallback traces, and confirm auth success rate. If green at 10% in 30m we promote to 100% and notify customer. Also opening INC ticket INC-7893.

maya_prod: noted. I'll draft customer communication: temporary mitigation in progress; requesting billing hold until we confirm impact.

dave_sre: added a short-term guard in the proxy: whitelist any x-*region headers if present so this doesn't regress on future hygiene patches. Follow-up PR inbound.

carla_support: thanks team — please paste canary metrics here. I'll loop in account manager and support ENG lead. :eyes:
